03 / Independent project

Memory Applicability Guard

A Python prototype that reviews whether an old memory should influence an agent's next answer or action.

Role
Independent project
When
May–August 2026
Tools
Python, JSON, unit tests
The project

The problem

Memory can help an assistant remember useful context. It can also carry an old permission, a fact that has changed, or an instruction that does not belong in the current task. Retrieval alone cannot tell the agent whether to use it.

ExampleIf an old note says a user allowed an action and the current request revokes that permission, the old note should no longer guide the action.

What I built

I made a deterministic Python helper and packaged it as an installable agent skill. Given structured inputs, it recommends whether the memory should be used, ignored, or clarified. The output records the decisive evidence, a reason code, and a next step.

It treats two questions separately: whether the memory applies, and what the agent should do with the task. The latter may call for proceeding, revising, asking the user, checking an external fact, or escalating for review.

What I learned

The related frozen v0.7 experiment did not outperform its baseline; both scored 110 out of 128. That result matters. The project is now framed as an auditable review workflow, not as a proven way to make autonomous agents safe.

The helper has deterministic tests and a public repository. It has not been validated as a production safety system.
